business_scope.primary_industry_name: Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) Ocean Box Brokerage

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: France (unitary semi-presidential republic; no sub-state corporate tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France-United States Income Tax Convention (signed 28 July 1967, as amended by Protocols of 2006 and 2009)
France-China Double Taxation and Anti-Fiscal-Evasion Convention (signed 30 November 1984, as subsequently amended by relevant protocols, with the OECD Multilateral Instrument applied)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier - CMF), Articles L561-1 to L561-50 and R561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT obligations, Tracfin reporting regime, customer due diligence and record-keeping duties); French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L561-45 to L561-49 (declaration of beneficial owners, Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE, included in the Registre National des Entreprises dossier); Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 5 February 2020 and Décret n° 2020-118 of 12 February 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843; Decree No. 2016-1602 of 24 November 2016 on practical RBE filing obligations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing and extract of the company register of each ultimate shareholder legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or Chamber of Commerce of the beneficial shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Hague Convention) for all contracting states; otherwise full Consular Legalization through the French Embassy or Consulate competent for the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized powers of attorney and corporate authorization resolutions empowering the natural-person signatories of the draft articles of association (projet de statuts)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's country of origin or French notary where the instrument is executed in France
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; where the country of origin is non-signatory to the 1961 Hague Convention, Consular Legalization by the French consular post

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of each UBO and of the proposed President (Président) of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing police or civil registry authority, or notary public of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague countries, consular certification by the French Consulate; notarial certification acceptable where the French filing pack expressly permits it

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and professional solvency attestation supporting the NVOCC financial guarantee and DGDDI customs broker (déclarant en douane) authorization file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originating credit institution or authorized surety/insurer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the issuing bank or surety's signature for foreign origin documents

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and ongoing screening of each direct and indirect beneficial owner, all proposed officers and every authorized signatory against: (i) Tracfin and French asset-freezing orders (gel des avoirs) issued by the Direction Générale du Trésor under CMF Articles L562-1 et seq.; (ii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions Database (CFSD) and all restrictive-measures regulations in force, including Regulation (EU) 833/2014 and successor acts; (iv) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, which is mandatory where USD-denominated Swift wire or correspondent-banking rails are used; and (v) the national PEP file maintained by Tracfin and the politically exposed person definition of CMF Article L561-2-2. Screening evidence must be dated and retained for five years from the end of the business relationship (CMF Article L561-12-1); failure to file a suspicious transaction report (déclaration de soupçon) where required by CMF Article L561-15 exposes the entity and its directors to the penalty regime of CMF Articles L561-21 to L561-24.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by INPI - Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; search and data checks: data.inpi.fr), with the final name insertion effected in the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) and the proof of registration extracted as the Kbis from the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (dénomination sociale) must be written in Latin alphabet characters (UTF-8 encoding) compliant with the French public-order rules; statutory instruments and public documents issued in France must be in French under the Toubon Law (Law No. 94-665 of 4 August 1994); foreign-language or non-Roman-script elements are acceptable only if transliterated into Roman letters and reviewed by INPI for identity or confusion risk; legal-form abbreviations such as 'SAS', 'SA' or 'SARL' must correspond exactly to the actual entity form selected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Crédit, Caisse d'épargne and assimilated banking tokens - prior approval of the Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority (ACPR) required
Assurance, Réassurance, Mutuelle - reserved for ACPR-licensed insurance and mutual entities
République, France (when implying state institution), National, Ministère, Préfecture, Police, Gendarmerie, Armée - reserved for public authorities and requiring prior ministerial consent
Notaire, Avocat, Commissaire de justice, Médecin, Pharmacien, Expert-comptable, Commissaire aux comptes - reserved for regulated professions subject to professional order rules
Syndicat, Fédération, Union, Coopérative - confined to genuine associative, union or cooperative entities
Croix-Rouge and other emblems protected by the Geneva Conventions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice issued by the Guichet unique (INPI) stating the conflict grounds (identity with an existing RNE entry, trademark infringement or font of public order), the applicant may: (i) verify the cited conflict in the RNE and INPI trademark databases; (ii) file a reasoned administrative reconsideration request (recours gracieux) through the Guichet unique portal within 15 days of the notification; (iii) if refused, institute judicial proceedings before the competent civil or commercial court (Tribunal judiciaire or Tribunal de commerce depending on the legal head of challenge) within 30 days of the rejection response; and (iv) in trademark-based rejections, alternatively pursue INPI trademark opposition cancellation or written consent of the prior rights holder. Interim relief (référé) before the Tribunal de commerce is available where imminent and irreparable harm is demonstrated.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for purely administrative registration: a SAS may domicile its registered office (siège social) at an approved corporate domiciliation company registered under Articles L123-11-1 to L123-11-3 of the French Commercial Code for an initial period of up to five years, renewable, subject to a compliant domiciliation agreement including letterhead obligations. However, where the SAS seeks DGDDI authorization as a customs broker (déclarant en douane) under the French Customs Code, French administrative practice requires professional premises in France accessible to customs inspection; a pure virtual office is deficient for the NVOCC licensing component and an operational physical hub or contracted sub-agent premises in France (for example at Le Havre, Marseille or Paris-CDG gateway) is indispensable to demonstrate genuine commercial substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified annualized inspection risk: 20-30% for a standard non-regulated SAS registered office; 45-65% for the NVOCC operating address once DGDDI customs broker authorization is in force, owing to unannounced on-site verification powers of the customs administration and Tracfin's communication and control rights under CMF Article L561-38; ACPR on-site visits are not methodologically expected for this commercial entity class but cannot be wholly excluded if ancillary banking activity is identified.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory incorporation filing and RNE registration fee (Guichet unique/INPI administrative formalities, fixed greffe duty, chancellery fee and issuance of the Kbis extract)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RNE registration) collecting via the Guichet unique operated by INPI
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff fixed by decree of the French Ministry of Justice (regulated greffe fees adjusted by Arrêté of 28 February 2020)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory publication of the incorporation notice (avis de constitution) in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized to receive legal notices
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Authorized legal announcements gazette (journal habilité à recevoir les annonces légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, EUR 120-350 per insertion depending on gazette type and lineage

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication and apostille/consular legalization bundle for foreign corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in the country of origin plus the relevant French Embassy or Consulate where consular legalization applies
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff of the country of origin plus the French consular fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified legal translation into French of the foreign Kbis equivalents, certificates of good standing, identity documents and powers of attorney (bundle of five source documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-certified translator (traducteur assermenté) registered with a Cour d'appel in France
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark at EUR 50-90 per source page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate domiciliation service (registered office provider) - annual fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) registered under Article L123-11-3 of the French Commercial Code
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, EUR 100-300 per month depending on mail handling and reception package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal advisory: drafting of the SAS articles of association (statuts), UBO declaration (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs), corporate governance annexes, governance policy and filing checklist
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French avocat (law firm admitted to a French bar)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, EUR 2,000-4,500 flat fee in the Paris market for SAS formation including pre-incorporation due diligence

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Financial guarantee premium (caution bancaire or surety) for the NVOCC customs broker authorization and freight forwarding security requirements under French customs practice - first annual premium
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Credit institution or approved insurance surety accepted by DGDDI; DGDDI file processing at the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of 0.5%-2.0% of the guaranteed amount scaled to projected freight turnover; statutory solvency and guarantee conditions of the French Customs Code

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS) and Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general provisions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) within the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier de création d'entreprise (incorporation file) including statuts (articles of association) and déclaration de conformité (declaration of compliance)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SAS; however, if the capital is set below €1, it must be fully paid up at incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited in a blocked bank account (compte bloqué) until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders of the SAS, approve the incorporation and adopt the articles of association. RESOLVED, that the share capital of €[amount] be subscribed and paid as per the articles, and that the capital be deposited in a blocked account. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [address]. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed as President of the SAS, with full authority to represent the company and execute all legal documents. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed as General Manager, if applicable. RESOLVED, that the President is authorized to complete all formalities for registration with the RCS, to publish legal notices, and to open bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders and legal counsel (notary optional unless real estate contribution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts (articles of association) in French, specifying corporate name, registered office, share capital, share distribution, and management structure. All shareholders must sign the statuts. If a notary is required (e.g., for real estate contributions), ensure notarization.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of registered office (e.g., lease agreement or ownership title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the statuts are rejected by the registry for incompleteness, amend and re-sign as necessary; consult legal counsel for compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish Legal Notice in a Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal gazette (e.g., Les Affiches Parisiennes)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice of incorporation in a legal gazette (journal d'annonces légales) authorized in the department of the registered office. The notice must include the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, and purpose.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the gazette rejects the notice due to formatting, correct and resubmit; ensure compliance with legal publication requirements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Share Capital in a Blocked Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any French bank (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account (compte bloqué) in the name of the company in formation and deposit the cash portion of the share capital. Obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) from the bank.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to open the account, provide additional documentation or choose another bank; ensure the certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossier with the Commercial Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation dossier to the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the registered office's jurisdiction. The dossier includes the statuts, legal notice, bank certificate, declaration of compliance, and other required forms. Pay the filing fee.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (e.g., missing document), respond within 15 days by providing the requested information; otherwise, the application may be rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain K-bis Extract and Register with INSEE
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce and INSEE (National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the registry issues an extract K-bis (official proof of registration) and assigns a SIREN number. The company is automatically registered with INSEE for statistical purposes. Verify the K-bis details and retain for legal and banking purposes.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is delayed, contact the registry; if errors are found, request correction immediately.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de la Transition écologique et de la Cohésion des territoires – Direction Générale des Infrastructures, des Transports et des Mobilités (DGITM)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licence de commissionnaire de transport (freight forwarding license)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Déclaration) – low environmental impact for office-based operations
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with EU and French wastewater, air emission, and waste management standards; office operations typically exempt from full discharge permits, but must adhere to local municipal waste disposal and water discharge regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (attestation de sécurité incendie) from the local fire department, structural load inspection for any warehouse or storage area, and workplace occupational health and safety clearance from the labor inspectorate (Inspection du travail).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), including the competent Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE). Principal online portal: impots.gouv.fr and the professional tax account (espace professionnel). Customs and import-export VAT matters are administered through the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI), principally via the French customs online systems and the European Union Customs Trader Portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS obtains its French SIREN and SIRET identifiers through registration with the competent business formalities authority via the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). The DGFiP then allocates or confirms the corporate income tax account and, where applicable, the intra-Community VAT identification number. The company must establish a professional tax account on impots.gouv.fr, provide its incorporation extract, registered office details, legal representative information, bank details, business activity description, and expected turnover, and submit the appropriate VAT liability or exemption declarations. A non-resident entity conducting taxable transactions in France must appoint a French fiscal representative where required by applicable VAT rules, unless established in an EU Member State or otherwise covered by an applicable relief. A non-EU entity generally registers through the Foreign Businesses Tax Service (Service des impôts des entreprises étrangères) and may require a French fiscal representative for VAT compliance. Operators importing or exporting goods must also obtain an Economic Operators Registration and Identification number (EORI) from French customs. A VAT number is generally structured as FR plus a two-digit validation key and the entity's nine-digit SIREN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS) at entity level. There is no general US-style check-the-box election. An eligible SAS may elect temporary taxation under the personal income tax regime (impôt sur le revenu, or IR) for a maximum period of five fiscal years if statutory conditions are satisfied, including qualifying ownership, size, age, commercial activity, and shareholder participation requirements. The election must be made within the prescribed period and is generally irrevocable after the applicable deadline. A qualifying SAS may also participate in a French tax consolidation regime with qualifying French subsidiaries under statutory ownership and election conditions. VAT grouping may be available for closely linked French entities, but it is a separate indirect-tax election and does not change the SAS corporate income tax classification. French anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement the EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive framework and can deny deductions, impose inclusion, or restrict exemption where an arrangement produces a hybrid mismatch; they do not provide a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or VAT), supplemented by customs duties and import VAT. France does not use a general state-level sales and use tax system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no single universal VAT registration threshold for all activities. The French franchise en base regime generally applies to domestic turnover below the applicable statutory threshold. For services, including most freight-forwarding and brokerage services, the principal annual threshold is EUR 37,500, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 41,250 under the applicable current rules. For sales of goods and related activities, the principal threshold is generally EUR 85,000, with a tolerance threshold of EUR 93,500. Thresholds are subject to statutory indexation and must be verified for the relevant tax year. These thresholds do not eliminate VAT obligations arising from imports, intra-Community acquisitions, reverse-charge transactions, or specific place-of-supply rules. A freight forwarder may therefore require VAT registration even when domestic turnover is below the franchise threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has adopted a staged mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction-data reporting framework. The framework uses an approved public invoicing portal and/or registered private dematerialization platforms (plateformes de dématérialisation partenaires, or PDPs). It is not currently a universal real-time invoice-clearance system for all transactions. The scheduled framework requires all French-established businesses to be able to receive electronic invoices from 1 September 2026, with mandatory issuance and transaction-data reporting phased by business size, generally from 1 September 2026 for large and medium-sized businesses and from 1 September 2027 for small and micro-enterprises, subject to legislative or regulatory changes. Domestic business-to-business invoices within the scope of French VAT must use the prescribed structured or hybrid electronic formats and transmit required data through the approved channel. E-reporting applies principally to specified business-to-consumer and cross-border transactions. Import and export customs documentation remains subject to separate DGDDI electronic customs systems. There is no general requirement for a French VAT digital stamp on every invoice, but invoices must contain the mandatory legal particulars and be retained in an auditable electronic form.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: France generally applies VAT exemption with a right of deduction, rather than a domestic 0% rate, to qualifying exports of goods outside the European Union. The exporter must demonstrate that the goods left the EU customs territory, that the transaction is made by or on behalf of an eligible exporter, and that the customs export formalities were correctly completed. The primary evidence is the electronic export declaration and the customs confirmation of exit, normally identified through the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and exit results. Services must be analyzed under the place-of-supply rules rather than automatically treated as exports. A business-to-business service supplied to a customer established outside France is generally located where the customer is established and may be outside the scope of French VAT, subject to customer-status evidence and anti-abuse rules. International transport and certain services directly connected with exports, imports, or international transport may qualify for specific French VAT exemptions where the statutory conditions and documentary evidence are satisfied. Freight-forwarding, NVOCC, brokerage, warehousing, documentation, and ancillary services must be analyzed separately; an invoice described as an export service is insufficient by itself. For VAT recovery, the claimant must retain valid purchase invoices, customs evidence, transport records, contracts, customer identification, proof of service, and records supporting the applicable place-of-supply or exemption rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic customs export declaration accepted by French customs or the relevant EU customs authority, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Customs confirmation that the goods exited the European Union customs territory, including the exit results or equivalent electronic exit evidence
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the exporter, consignee, goods, value, delivery terms, and transaction reference
Bill of lading, sea waybill, or other carrier transport document for ocean freight
Freight-forwarding or NVOCC contract, booking confirmation, house bill of lading, master bill of lading, and delivery or loading evidence where applicable
Evidence linking the invoice to the customs declaration and exported goods
Customer and establishment evidence supporting the applicable business-to-business place-of-supply rule for offshore services
Proof of payment and accounting records where relevant to audit substantiation
Inward remittance certificate only where required by a bank, financing arrangement, or non-French foreign-exchange documentation regime; it is not a general French VAT zero-rating prerequisite
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general foreign-exchange control requiring export proceeds to be repatriated within 180 days. VAT exemption or recovery may be denied or clawed back if the taxpayer cannot prove export, EU exit, customer status, taxable use, or the statutory connection between the service and the export or international transport. The DGFiP may assess unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, and applicable tax penalties, including penalties for insufficient documentation, intentional non-compliance, or fraudulent conduct. Fraudulent VAT claims may also trigger administrative fines, criminal prosecution, liability of directors or officers, and recovery of improperly refunded VAT. Customs irregularities may result in post-clearance duty and import-VAT assessments, customs penalties, seizure or forfeiture measures, and liability under the Union Customs Code and French customs law. Repeated or material non-compliance can lead to denial of simplified procedures, enhanced customs controls, loss of trusted-trader status, and increased audit scrutiny. Records supporting exports, transport, invoicing, and VAT treatment should generally be retained for the applicable French statutory limitation period, commonly three years for VAT assessment purposes, subject to longer periods for fraud, criminal matters, customs records, and corporate accounting documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) and the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) under the authority of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Recovery; foreign exchange policy is coordinated with the European Central Bank (ECB) for euro-zone matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full member of the eurozone; the euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. There are no general exchange controls on capital movements within the EU/EEA, and profit remittances (dividends, branch profits) are freely transferable subject to standard corporate documentation and anti-money laundering (AML) verification. Non-resident shareholders may receive dividends without prior authorization, but must provide proof of beneficial ownership and tax residency to avoid withholding tax issues. For transactions with non-EU/EEA countries, France applies EU-wide sanctions and targeted asset freezes, but no blanket convertibility restrictions. The only practical hurdles are documentary: banks require underlying commercial contracts, invoices, and customs declarations to process cross-border payments, and may apply enhanced due diligence for high-risk jurisdictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France does not impose mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency earnings in foreign currency accounts (comptes en devises) or convert them to EUR at market rates. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation of export receipts; however, for customs and VAT purposes, export transactions must be settled within the standard commercial terms (typically 90-180 days) to avoid reclassification as a domestic supply. The Banque de France requires statistical reporting for balance-of-payments purposes on a monthly basis for transactions exceeding €50,000, but this is a reporting obligation, not a surrender requirement. No mandatory conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Compte de dépôt) and optionally a Capital Escrow Account for initial share capital if required by the bank's internal policy
Operational Account (Compte courant professionnel) and dedicated FX settlement account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole CIB (Corporate and Investment Banking)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Trade Finance Account (for LC and guarantees)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. French-regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Shine, and Lydia Pro offer multi-currency accounts and SWIFT/SEPA transfers, but they are not full-service banks and may have lower transaction limits for high-volume NVOCC operations. They are viable for operational liquidity and FX conversion, but for large trade settlements (LCs, large wire transfers) a tier-1 bank is recommended. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise Business) are permitted to operate in France under EU passporting, but they are subject to the same AML/KYC requirements and may not provide local French IBANs (though they can provide French IBANs via partner banks). Legal constraints: EMIs cannot provide credit facilities or issue guarantees; they are not covered by the French deposit guarantee scheme (FGDR) for funds held beyond the e-money threshold. For NVOCC operations requiring high-volume disbursements, a hybrid approach (tier-1 bank + EMI for FX) is viable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a corporate entity. French banks mandate that at least one director (or a designated signatory with power of attorney) appear in person at a branch to verify identity and sign the account opening agreement. Remote opening is possible for certain banks (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale) via video identification, but this is subject to the bank's internal policy and the risk profile of the entity. For an NVOCC (medium-risk), most banks will require a physical meeting or a notarized power of attorney if the director is non-resident. The KYC interview (entretien) is mandatory to discuss the business model, expected transaction volumes, and source of funds. For non-resident directors, a physical visit to France or a French embassy/consulate for identity verification may be required. Some banks allow video conferencing with a notary, but this is not universal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure (e.g., payments to/from sanctioned or high-risk countries for freight forwarding)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed compliance policy, including: (1) list of sanctioned countries and prohibited parties (UN/EU/OFAC) screened against all counterparties; (2) copies of export/import licenses and customs declarations; (3) underlying commercial contracts and invoices for each transaction; (4) proof of due diligence on shipping partners and consignees (e.g., KYC on beneficial owners); (5) a written commitment to implement transaction monitoring and to report suspicious transactions to Tracfin (French FIU).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns (e.g., rapid in-and-out flows, high volume of small payments, or round amounts)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a business plan explaining the NVOCC model: (1) sample bill of lading and freight invoices; (2) explanation of payment cycles (e.g., prepayment to carriers, collection from shippers); (3) accounting records showing matching of receivables and payables; (4) a cash flow forecast; (5) evidence of physical office and operational substance (lease, employee contracts).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity (e.g., non-resident shareholders or complex corporate structure)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full corporate structure chart with ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) identified; certified copies of passports and proof of address; notarized articles of association; a declaration of the source of funds for the initial capital injection; and a commitment to update UBO registry (RCS) within 30 days of any change.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of physical presence or substance (shell company risk)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a lease agreement for a registered office in France, employment contracts for at least one local employee (or a management company), utility bills, and a detailed description of operational activities (e.g., warehouse contracts, carrier agreements).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For initial capital injection from a non-resident shareholder: use SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from the shareholder's bank to the French SAS's operational account. The payment must include a clear purpose code (e.g., 'Capital contribution' or 'Shareholder loan') and reference the company's SIREN number. For amounts exceeding €10,000, the bank will require a copy of the share subscription agreement and proof of the shareholder's identity. For capital contributions in kind (e.g., equipment), a notarized valuation is required. The French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) requires statistical reporting for direct investment flows (including capital injections) if the amount exceeds €15,000 per transaction; the bank will handle this reporting. For loans from shareholders, a loan agreement with interest rate and repayment schedule must be provided to avoid reclassification as hidden equity. The bank will verify the source of funds (e.g., bank statements) to comply with AML.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements (e.g., paying ocean carriers, port charges, or overseas agents), the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for wire transfers. For larger transactions or when a documentary credit is required, a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) can be issued via the bank's trade finance department. For EU/EEA payments, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) is used, but for non-EU payments, SWIFT is standard. The bank will require supporting documents: commercial invoice, bill of lading, and customs declaration (for exports). For payments to high-risk jurisdictions, additional due diligence is required. The NVOCC may also use ACH Direct (SEPA Direct Debit) for recurring payments to domestic suppliers, but this is not typical for cross-border. For FX conversion, the bank will execute at the interbank rate plus a margin; alternatively, the company can use a fintech EMI for better rates.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward contracts (FX forwards) with a maturity up to 12 months, available from tier-1 banks for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other major currencies, subject to a credit line and underlying exposure documentation.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies with restricted convertibility (e.g., CNY, INR) are permissible but only through banks with a license to trade in those markets; the French bank will act as an intermediary.
Currency swaps (FX swaps) for simultaneous spot and forward transactions, used to manage liquidity in multiple currencies, available from banks with a treasury desk.

Options (FX options) are permissible but require a more sophisticated risk management framework and are typically used by larger NVOCCs; they are not listed in the schema but are allowed under French regulations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard corporate income tax is 25%. Qualifying small companies may apply a 15% rate to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit, generally subject to turnover not exceeding EUR 10 million, paid-in capital being fully paid, and at least 75% individual ownership. There is no general corporate tax holiday. Research and development tax credits, apprenticeship credits, and other sector-specific credits may reduce the effective burden. Tax losses may generally be carried forward indefinitely, subject to an annual utilization cap of EUR 1 million plus 50% of the portion of current-year profit exceeding EUR 1 million. A tax loss carryback election is generally available for the immediately preceding financial year, subject to statutory limits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited; France does not apply a five-year expiry rule. Annual utilization is capped as described above.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD for the corporate income tax return, supported by the relevant 2058-A to 2058-C tax computation schedules, 2059-A to 2059-G determination schedules, and 2050 to 2057 balance-sheet and income-statement schedules. Electronic filing is generally made through the DGFiP EDI-TDFC system using an authorized electronic filing provider. Certain taxpayers may use the impots.gouv.fr professional portal where available.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual corporate income tax return; quarterly or periodic advance payments are separate payment obligations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a financial year ending on 31 December, the return is generally due by the second working day following 1 May of the following year, subject to the applicable electronic-filing calendar. For a financial year ending on another date, the return is generally due within three months after the financial year-end. Corporate income tax installments are generally due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September, and 15 December, with the final balance generally due by the 15th day of the fourth month following year-end. For a 31 December year-end, the balance is generally due by 15 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, French SIREN number, registered office, tax office, financial year opening and closing dates, and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the French SAS legal entity as the taxpayer. Identify foreign shareholders, parent entities, and any foreign permanent establishment or branch information where requested. Do not substitute the foreign parent for the French SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result, corporate income tax due, credits, reductions, installment payments, and balance payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the French entity's standalone taxable result unless a valid French tax consolidation regime applies. Exclude foreign-parent income not legally attributable to the SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from accounting profit or loss to taxable profit or loss, including permanent add-backs, deductions, non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation adjustments, and tax-exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible related-party charges, unsupported management fees, excessive interest, penalties, gifts, and expenses lacking a French business purpose. Document cross-border charges and withholding tax treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward, losses utilized in the current year, and remaining losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the French annual utilization cap. Maintain schedules demonstrating the origin, amount, and continuity of losses. Do not assume foreign-group losses are available to the SAS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, reductions, and other items reducing corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by statutory eligibility and contemporaneous evidence. Foreign tax credits require a valid legal basis and supporting foreign tax documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of taxable profit, capital gains, participation-related items, and allocation of certain tax components.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify gains, securities income, participation exemptions, and extraordinary items under French rules. Apply participation exemptions only where statutory ownership and holding-period conditions are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet, income statement, fixed assets, depreciation, provisions, receivables, liabilities, expenses, and related accounting data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use French statutory accounts or compliant tax-accounting data. Reconcile freight revenue, pass-through carrier costs, commissions, customer advances, demurrage, foreign currency items, and intercompany balances.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of certain extraordinary or non-deductible expenses, including specified remuneration and other regulated categories.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose relevant payments to directors, related parties, and foreign group entities where the form requires it. Preserve board approvals and commercial evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Relevant withholding taxes, distributions, and tax credits connected with payments or distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, and other outbound payments with withholding returns, treaty claims, beneficial-owner evidence, and payment ledgers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research tax credit claim, where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only for qualifying French or eligible European Union/EEA research activities supported by technical files, personnel records, costs, and subcontractor evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual summary of related-party transactions and transfer-pricing information where the taxpayer is within the applicable French reporting scope.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose material cross-border transactions with the foreign parent and affiliates, including services, financing, royalties, guarantees, and commissions. Reconcile values to the general ledger and Local File.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Information on related-party transactions, tax-group status, controlled entities, and foreign operations where required by the relevant schedules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the ultimate parent, direct shareholders, controlled entities, tax-consolidation status, and any foreign permanent establishment or controlled foreign company exposure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, increased to 40% where a formal notice is not complied with and potentially 80% in cases of fraudulent conduct or abusive tax behavior. Interest for late payment is generally 0.20% per month, subject to statutory rules. Failure to file, incomplete filing, inaccurate filing, or failure to provide transfer-pricing documentation can trigger separate fixed or percentage-based penalties. Tax assessment may be increased by interest and applicable penalties. Electronic filing failures can also result in penalties where electronic filing is mandatory.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: The standard French withholding tax on dividends paid by a French company to a non-resident corporate shareholder is generally 25%, subject to applicable exemptions and tax treaties. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply to qualifying EU corporate parents meeting ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, anti-abuse, and beneficial-ownership conditions. A domestic participation exemption may also apply in specific qualifying situations.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a current certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority, verify treaty residence, beneficial ownership, legal form, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse requirements where relevant, and confirm that the recipient is not an artificial conduit. Apply the reduced treaty rate only where French administrative procedures permit relief at source. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and file a refund claim using the applicable French forms, commonly forms 5000 and 5001 for treaty relief. Maintain shareholder registers, ownership evidence, payment records, residence certificates, treaty analysis, and anti-abuse support. Treaty relief is not available solely because the recipient is incorporated in a treaty jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic withholding on royalties and similar payments to non-residents is generally 25%, subject to treaty reduction, EU Interest and Royalties Directive relief, and statutory exemptions. Interest paid by a French company to a non-resident is generally not subject to ordinary French withholding tax, subject to anti-abuse rules, payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions or territories, and specific statutory exceptions. Payments to a non-cooperative jurisdiction or territory may be subject to a punitive 75% rate for relevant interest, royalty, and similar income. Treaty rates vary by recipient jurisdiction and payment classification. Beneficial ownership, substance, arm's-length pricing, treaty eligibility, and anti-conduit evidence are required.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: French full transfer-pricing documentation, including a Master File and Local File, is generally mandatory where the French entity or French tax group has annual pre-tax turnover or gross assets of at least EUR 400 million, or where it is controlled by, controls, or is part of an entity or tax group meeting the statutory EUR 400 million threshold. Certain transactions and groups below that threshold remain subject to the arm's-length principle, record-keeping, and information-production obligations. Country-by-Country Reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no separate United Arab Emirates-style Economic Substance Regulations regime. Substance is nevertheless material under French transfer-pricing rules, the general anti-abuse rule, the principal-purpose anti-abuse rule, beneficial-ownership requirements, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, and judicial doctrines concerning abuse of law and abnormal act of management. A French SAS should maintain real French decision-making, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or operational infrastructure, commercial risk control, bank-account control, books and records, and evidence that freight-forwarding functions and risks are actually performed in France. A contractual commissionaire or NVOCC structure must be consistent with actual conduct and risk allocation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Tax Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing freight-forwarding revenue, fabricating expenses, maintaining double books, deducting personal or non-business expenditure, understating customs-related income, or intentionally filing false corporate tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, late-payment interest, tax penalties generally ranging from 10% to 80%, and criminal tax-fraud penalties that may include imprisonment of up to five years and a fine of up to EUR 500,000. Aggravated cases can carry up to seven years' imprisonment and a fine of up to EUR 3 million, with higher limits in specified organized or aggravated circumstances. Legal entities may face substantially increased fines, confiscation, publication, and exclusion from public contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability, civil liability, personal tax liability under the French tax-director liability procedure where fraudulent or repeated conduct makes collection impossible, and management bans. Confiscation and restitution may apply. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be ordered through criminal procedure or judicial control.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting fictitious freight invoices, falsely treating domestic services as exports, misclassifying import VAT, claiming unsupported input VAT, or participating in fraudulent intra-EU invoice chains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recovery of unpaid VAT, late-payment interest, penalties commonly up to 40% for deliberate failure and up to 80% for fraudulent or abusive conduct, possible criminal prosecution, and suspension or restriction of VAT-related rights. Criminal penalties may include imprisonment and fines depending on the offense and aggravating circumstances.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers may be prosecuted for intentional participation, fraudulent bookkeeping, or complicity. Personal civil exposure can arise where management misconduct causes tax loss, and criminal courts may impose confiscation, professional prohibitions, and restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating customs value, falsifying origin, misclassifying goods, misusing preferential origin, concealing cargo, or providing inaccurate data to customs brokers and carriers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Customs reassessment, seizure or forfeiture, customs fines, interest, loss of customs simplifications or authorizations, and potential criminal prosecution. Sanctions depend on the Customs Code offense, the goods, intent, and the value of the evaded duties or prohibited goods.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible employees may be personally prosecuted for intentional customs fraud or complicity. The SAS, its customs representative, and involved individuals may face joint or separate penalties, confiscation, and loss of authorization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unsupported management fees, artificial royalty charges, non-arm's-length financing, shifting freight margins to a foreign affiliate, failing to document intercompany services, or maintaining contractual terms inconsistent with actual functions and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment to arm's-length profit, denial of deductions, withholding-tax exposure, interest, penalties, and transfer-pricing documentation penalties. Failure to produce required documentation can result in a penalty based on the greater of a statutory minimum and a percentage of the reassessed profits or transactions, subject to applicable limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face liability for deliberate misrepresentation, fraudulent accounting, abuse of corporate assets, or tax fraud. Mere non-arm's-length pricing without intent does not automatically create criminal personal liability, but repeated or deliberate manipulation materially increases exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared Permanent Establishment or Agency Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A foreign parent or affiliate habitually concluding contracts, negotiating essential terms, controlling customers, or conducting core NVOCC and freight-forwarding functions in France without appropriate French registration, tax reporting, or profit attribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French corporate income tax, VAT, payroll tax, business taxes, interest, penalties, and possible reassessment of the foreign enterprise's French taxable profit. Employment, transport, customs, and regulatory sanctions may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be exposed for deliberate evasion, misleading filings, unlawful management, and failure to comply with French registration or licensing requirements. A French SAS does not shield individuals from their own criminal acts or serious management misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend, Interest, and Royalty Withholding-Tax Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a foreign shareholder or affiliate without withholding, applying a treaty rate without a valid residence certificate, treating a royalty as a service fee, or routing payments through a conduit lacking beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the unpaid withholding tax against the French payer, late-payment interest, penalties, possible 40% or 80% increases depending on conduct, and denial of treaty relief. The payer may remain liable even where the recipient received the gross payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable in cases of deliberate withholding-tax evasion, fraudulent payment instructions, or insolvency caused by misconduct. Criminal exposure may arise for falsification, fraud, or complicity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SAS as a nominal invoicing vehicle, lacking real French activity, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, routing funds through nominee shareholders, or creating artificial entities to obtain treaty, VAT, customs, or tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, abuse-of-law reassessment, tax penalties, beneficial-owner reporting violations, possible dissolution or administrative consequences, confiscation, and criminal sanctions for fraud or money laundering where applicable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, de facto managers, nominees, and beneficial owners may face criminal prosecution, confiscation, management bans, civil restitution, and liability for tax and creditor losses. Travel bans or passport restrictions require a specific judicial or criminal-procedure order and are not automatic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, bypassing customer identification, ignoring sanctions or adverse-media alerts, structuring payments, concealing beneficial ownership, or failing to report suspicious activity where a regulated intermediary obligation applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory measures, administrative fines, professional restrictions, account or transaction freezes, confiscation, and criminal money-laundering penalties. Aggravated money laundering can carry severe imprisonment and fines, with enhanced consequences for organized activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be personally liable for intentional participation, facilitation, concealment, or obstruction. Failure to maintain appropriate controls may also cause civil claims, banking termination, and loss of commercial authorizations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing payments, brokering cargo, or providing logistics services involving sanctioned persons, embargoed destinations, prohibited goods, or evasion structures without screening and authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Asset freezes, transaction prohibitions, administrative and criminal fines, imprisonment depending on the applicable sanctions regime, confiscation, and loss of customs or trade privileges.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and employees may be prosecuted personally for intentional violations, circumvention, or facilitation. Corporate status does not protect individuals from sanctions-related criminal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Corporate Assets and Insolvency Misconduct
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Diverting company funds to shareholders or related parties, paying sham consulting fees, making unlawful distributions, preferring insiders during insolvency, or continuing to trade while knowingly unable to pay debts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Repayment, damages, clawback of transactions, bankruptcy or liquidation proceedings, director contribution to insufficient assets, management bans, and criminal sanctions for abuse of corporate assets or bankruptcy offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS liability shield does not protect directors from personal liability for faute de gestion, abuse of corporate assets, fraudulent insolvency, or intentional wrongdoing. Civil restitution, asset seizure, management prohibitions, and imprisonment may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a French freight transport commissionnaire or performing regulated forwarding activity without required registration, professional capacity, financial standing, insurance, or compliance with transport and customs rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative orders, fines, suspension or withdrawal of registration, prohibition on operating, contract and insurance consequences, and potential criminal sanctions for unauthorized activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The president and de facto managers may be personally prosecuted for knowingly operating without required authorization or allowing regulated operations to continue after notice. Corporate liability does not eliminate individual responsibility for intentional breaches.
